segments.text: And so, now the way that we compute things with vectors typically is we introduce a coordinate system.

segments.text: So, if we're in the plane x, y axis, if we're in space, x, y, z axis, usually I will try to draw my x, y, z axis consistently to look like this.

segments.text: And then I can represent my vector in terms of its coordinates along the coordinate axis.

segments.text: So, that means when I have this arrow, I can ask how much does it go in the x direction, how much does it go in the y direction, how much does it go in the z direction?

segments.text: And so, for example, let's call this a vector a.

segments.text: So, a small convention, when we have a vector quantity, we put an arrow on top to remind us that it's a vector.

segments.text: And so, we can express any vector in terms of its components. So, the other notation is a1, a2, a3 between these square brackets.
